spans.text: And now that we are firm in our conviction that Hashem has chosen us, has taken care of us, will take care of us, and is the only power Who controls all elements of our lives, we come before Him with our requests—so that we will have all we need in order to do our unique part in this great mission in the best way possible.
FAQ: Honestly, I don't really care that much about my unique mission in this world—I just daven because I need stuff from Hashem. Is that so bad?
ANSWER: Very honest question! See Appendix 8.

(אֲדֹנָי, שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וּפִי יַגִּיד תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ—I am standing here because I do want to daven, create a relationship, and thank You for all the good You do for me—which is sometimes hard to see or understand—and I want to ask You for the help I need. But that does not come easy to me for so many reasons. Therefore, I am asking, please) Hashem, open my lips and help me express myself properly.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything, You control everything, and have taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history starting from the time of the Avos. You are all-powerful, You shower us with acts of helpful kindness (even though at times it is hard to see that), and everything is Yours. When dealing with us, You take into account the good deeds of our ancestors, and (everything You do for us is in order to) bring Mashiach to us, their descendants, even if we do not deserve it!

מֶלֶךְ חָפֵץ בַּחַיִּים—Please, Hashem, remember us for life; זָכְרֵנוּ לְחַיִּים—for You are our King Who desires life; וְכָתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַחַיִּים—and write us in the book of life; לְמַעַנְךָ אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים—so that we may be able to continue to serve You and live up to our potential.
You — מֶלֶךְ עוֹזֵר וּמוֹשִׁיעַ וּמָגֵן are our King, You have the power to help us through our difficulties, to save us (from our physical and spiritual enemies), and to,
protect us (from evil). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה — You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם — You are the Protector of Avraham (and us, his descendants).
Hashem, אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם — Your power and rulership are permanent; You bring about Techiyas Hameisim (since our souls are eternal); and You have unlimited power to save us.

You — מְכַלְכֵּל חַיִּים בְּחֶסֶד take care of us with Your kindness; and with Your great mercy You revive the dead (literally, Techiyas Hameisim, and You also save those who are near physical or spiritual death); You support those who have

fallen (physically and spiritually); You heal the sick (both physically and emotionally ill) and free those in prison (whether in real prisons or trapped in their own sense of limitations); and You keep the covenant You made with our ancestors. There is no other power like You at all; You have total control over our lives and our ultimate salvation. (And that is why we are turning to You and only You with the upcoming requests in our Shemoneh Esrei.)
זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו—There is no one like You, our merciful Father; מִי כָמוֹךָ אַב הָרַחֲמִים—with mercy. בְּרַחֲמִים—Who remembers us, His creations, for life; לְחַיִּים

וְנֶאֱמַן אַתָּה לְהַחֲיוֹת מֵתִים—We have total faith that You will perform Techiyas Hameisim. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים—Who performs Techiyas Hameisim. (Even though it has not yet happened, we are so sure that it will happen that we say this brachah in the present tense!)

Unlike angels who have a higher understanding of Hashem, we humans cannot understand "Who" Hashem is—His very essence (represented by the word "אותו"). All we can perceive is what He does—referred to as "שמך." Nevertheless, in Kedushah we will praise Hashem like the angels do. Since we can only do this when we are at the level of a tzibbur—a unified community—we therefore only say this with a minyan.

נְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת שִׁמְךָ בָּעוֹלָם—Let us declare the kedushah of "שמך"—all that Hashem does in this world; כְּשֵׁם—just like שֶׁמַּקְדִּישִׁים אוֹתוֹ בִּשְׁמֵי מָרוֹם—the angels declare the kedushah of "אותו"—the essence of Hashem.
כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ—As the Navi tells us; וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל זֶה וְאָמַר—that one angel calls to the other (so that they all praise Hashem in unison) and say:

קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת—The sanctity of Hashem can be felt in all worlds, from the very highest world of angels down to the very lowest world, our material world; מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ—His Presence can be felt everywhere (though it requires effort and diligence in order to tap into it through Torah and mitzvos).
Correspondingly, other angels offer praise and declare (as we do now also):
The essence of Hashem is completely beyond us (even the highest angels); it is מִמְּקוֹמוֹ—from His place (up there, it all makes sense!).
In addition, it is written in Your holy words:

The Kingship of Hashem is for all eternity (He will always be there for us, unlike our mortal helpers); and אֱלֹהַיִךְ צִיּוֹן—Hashem has a special providence on Eretz Yisrael; לְדֹר וָדֹר—in all generations: our past and our future; הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!

We will proclaim Your greatness and Your holiness from generation to generation, forever, because You are truly a great and Kadosh King. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the Almighty, the Kadosh One. (During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah say instead: הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the King, the Kadosh One.) (If you forgot—see Appendix 12:1)

You, Hashem, אַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ וְשִׁמְךָ קָדוֹשׁ are קָדוֹשׁ, separate and far removed from this physical world, and all that we see You do (וְשִׁמְךָ) is beyond our understanding. But we, Bnei Yisrael, are also קְדוֹשִׁים, separate and removed from the values and the norms of the regular material world (look at the miracle of our survival! And therefore, even though many times what happens to us seems not to make sense)—we, Your people, praise and thank You every day; בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the Almighty, the Kadosh One. (During Aseres Yemei Teshuvah say instead: הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ—the King, the Kadosh One.) (If you forgot—see Appendix 12:1)

Hashem,—אַתָּה חוֹנֵן לָאָדָם דַּעַת through Your kindness, You give mankind knowledge, and You teach us mere humans insight. Please grant us knowledge, understanding, and the intuitive sense to perceive
(right from wrong). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; חוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת—Who graciously gives (humans) knowledge.

Hashem, our—הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ אָבִינוּ לְתוֹרָתֶךָ Father, please lead us back to Your Torah; our King, please draw us close to be able to serve You and help us return to You with sincere and complete teshuvah. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה
יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָרוֹצֶה בִּתְשׁוּבָה—Who wants us to do (real and sincere) teshuvah.
—סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִינוּ כִּי חָטָאנוּ Hashem, our Father, please forgive us for we have sinned (through carelessness or weakness); our King, please pardon us for we have intentionally
sinned, because You pardon and forgive. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָֹה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; חַנּוּן הַמַּרְבֶּה לִסְלֹחַ—Who is gracious and forgives us repeatedly.
Hashem,—רְאֵה נָא בְעָנְיֵנוּ וְרִיבֵנוּ look at our suffering, defend our cause, and redeem us soon for the glory of Your Name (because when Bnei Yisrael suffer and are ridiculed, it
is a chillul Hashem), for You are a powerful Redeemer. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; גּוֹאֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who constantly redeems Bnei Yisrael.

עַנֵּנוּ—Please answer us on the day of public fasting for we are in great distress. We know we have not lived up to our potential, but please do not turn away from us! Rather, let Your great chessed be a comfort to us. Answer us even before we call out to You, as the pasuk says (when describing the end of days): "I (Hashem) answer their requests (that are in their hearts) even before they articulate them!" For You are the One Who answers us in times of our distress; You save and rescue us in all our times of trouble! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הָעוֹנֶה בְּעֵת צָרָה—Who answers in times of our distress.

רְפָאֵנוּ יְהֹוָה וְנֵרָפֵא—Hashem, please heal us, and then we will be truly healed; וְנִוּשָׁעָה—save us, and then we will be truly saved; כִּי תְהִלָּתֵנוּ אַתָּה—for we understand that the true praise for our recovery is due to You. And bring a complete healing to all our illnesses (physical and emotional).* For You, Hashem, are a faithful and merciful Healer. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; רוֹפֵא חוֹלֵי עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who heals the sick of His nation, Bnei Yisrael.

*One may insert now a tefillah for people who are ill: Please, Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, quickly send a complete recovery from Heaven, a spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery to (name) son/daughter of (mother's name) among the others of Bnei Yisrael who are in need of recovery.

בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, please bless this year and all its types of produce, so that we should be able to enjoy it and use it for good. And give us (in the summer say: a blessing) (in the winter say: rain and dew for a blessing) all over the earth, and may we be satisfied with all the good You give us! And please bless this year like the best of years. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מְבָרֵךְ הַשָּׁנִים—Who blesses the years.

תְּקַע—Hashem, sound the great shofar for our freedom, and raise up a banner (make a public demonstration of Your Divine Presence) in order to gather all our exiles, and gather us together from the four corners of the earth (to our Land). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מְקַבֵּץ נִדְחֵי עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who gathers the scattered of His nation, Bnei Yisrael.

הָשִׁיבָה—Restore our judges and those who guide us, as in earlier times, and remove from us sorrow and worry and confusion, and may You, Hashem alone, rule over us and guide us with kindness and compassion, and vindicate us in our judgment. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב—צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט—the King Who loves

And for those who slander (Bnei Yisrael), let there be no hope; and may all evil instantly be destroyed; and may all Your enemies and the enemies of Your nation be quickly cut down; and may You speedily uproot, crush, cast down, and humble all the arrogant, insolent, and intentional sinners swiftly in our days. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything;
שׁוֹבֵר אוֹיְבִים וּמַכְנִיעַ זֵדִים—Who destroys enemies and humbles the arrogant and the intentional sinners.

You, Hashem, Who controls everything, may Your mercy be aroused on all the tzaddikim, and on all the elders and leaders of Your nation, Bnei Yisrael, and also on all the righteous converts, and also on us! וְתֵן And—שָׂכָר טוֹב לְכָל הַבּוֹטְחִים בְּשִׁמְךָ בֶּאֱמֶת grant great reward to all who sincerely trust in You, and include us (who sometimes struggle with our bitachon) together with all of them; וְלֹא נֵבוֹשׁ—כִּי בְךָ בָטָחְנוּ and may we never feel embarrassed (to do the right thing), for we put our trust in You! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מִשְׁעָן וּמִבְטָח לַצַּדִיקִים—Who is the support and Source of trust for the tzaddikim.

—Hashem, even if we are not deserving, please return to Your city of Yerushalayim; and let Your Presence be felt there as You have promised; and rebuild it (the city and the Beis Hamikdash) soon, in our days, as an everlasting structure; and please (speedily) reestablish within it the throne of David HaMelech. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם—Who builds Yerushalayim (present tense—since every step of our galus is a necessary part of the process of the eventual permanent rebuilding of Yerushalayim).

—May Mashiach speedily appear; and may his power and glory be recognized by all, thanks to Your salvation; for we await and hope for Your salvation all day and every day. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; מַצְמִיחַ קֶרֶן—Who makes the power and glory of our salvation appear (present tense—just like the previous brachah).

—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, please listen to our voice, spare us, and have compassion on us; and accept our tefillos with mercy (if we are not really deserving); and with favor (if we are deserving); for You, Hashem, listen to tefillos and pleadings. Do not turn us away empty-handed from You, our King!

כִּי אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ—For You, Hashem, listen with compassion to the tefillos of Your nation, Bnei Yisrael (including me!). בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה—Who listens to tefillah.

רְצֵה יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל—You, Hashem, Who controls everything, be pleased with Your nation, Bnei Yisrael, and listen to their tefillos; וְהָשֵׁב and bring back the avodah in the Beis Hamikdash, and please accept their tefillos with love and favor, and all the mitzvos of Bnei Yisrael should always be favorable and acceptable to You.

Hashem,—אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, please view us favorably, and take into account our special relationship with You and the promises You made to our ancestors: the promise to bring Mashiach and to rebuild Yerushalayim and restore its holiness, and to remember all of Bnei Yisrael everywhere, to deliver us from our exiles (physical and spiritual), and to grant our requests and have mercy on us

(even if we are not deserving), and to give us all life and peace on this day of: Rosh Chodesh/Pesach/Sukkos. Give us all goodness, blessings, and life (even if we are not all deserving), show compassion on us, because we have turned to You for help, because we know that You, Hashem, control everything, and You are a compassionate and merciful King.

וְתֶחֱזֶינָה עֵינֵינוּ—May we personally merit seeing when Your Divine Presence returns to Zion. בָּרוּך—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַמַּחֲזִיר שְׁכִינָתוֹ—Who restores His Divine Presence to Zion. (Notice again the present tense! Every step in our galus is part of that process!)

מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ—We thank You, Hashem, for You are our God. You control everything, and You have taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history from the time of the Avos and forever and all time; צוּר חַיֵּינוּ מָגֵן—You are the rock of our lives and the protector Whom we rely upon. נוֹדֶה לְּךָ וּנְסַפֵּר תְּהִלָּתֶךָ—We thank You and speak Your praises, עַל חַיֵּינוּ—for our lives, which הַמְּסוּרִים בְּיָדֶיךָ—for our lives, which

are entrusted into Your Hand, and our souls, which are in Your care; וְעַל and for—נִסֵּיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם עִמָּנוּ Your (hidden) miracles that are with us every day (and we do not even realize it!); and for Your wonders and Your acts of goodness that occur at all times, evening, morning, and afternoon (literally, twenty-four hours a day, as well as figuratively, during the dark times in our lives, the clear bright times, and the hazy twilight times). הַטּוֹב—You are the Benevolent One, for Your compassion is never-ending; וְהַמְרַחֵם, כִּי לֹא תַמּוּ חֲסָדֶיךָ—You are the Merciful One, for Your loving-kindness is never exhausted. מֵעוֹלָם קִוִּינוּ לָךְ—From the beginning of time, we have placed our hope in You.

מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ—We thank You, Hashem, for You are our God. You control everything and have taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history starting from the time of the Avos. You are the Creator of all humanity, of the entire universe, and You specifically formed us as Your nation—for which we thank You, and for our miraculous survival till today. (And since we are so sure that Am Yisrael is eternal) כֵּן תְּחַיֵּינוּ וּתְקַיְּמֵנוּ—we thank You now for the fact that we will continue to survive, and that You will bring all the exiles to the (rebuilt) Beis Hamikdash where we will all serve You with a complete heart (with no doubts or questions). עַל שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ—We thank You for instilling in us the concept and (crucial) character trait of gratitude! בָּרוּךְ אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything, to Whom thanksgiving is due.

(וְ)—(We also thank You) for our miraculous rescue, for the mighty acts and victories, and for the battles (from which You allowed us to emerge victorious) that You performed for our ancestors in those days at this season.

In—בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ On Chanukah: In the days of the Kohen Gadol Matisyahu the Chashmonai and his children, the despotic Syrian-Greek empire rose up against Your people (Bnei Yisrael), to try to make them forget Your Torah and abandon the Torah way of life. But You, in Your great mercy, stood by the Torah-true Jews in their time of distress and championed their cause, defended their rights, and avenged the wrongs done to them. You made the weak and few (army of the Chashmonaim) victorious

over the stronger and more numerous (Greek army). You made the Jews who had remained pure from the immorality of the Greek culture (טְהוֹרִים), who had remained righteous and loyal to Torah standards (צַדִּיקִים), and who remained diligent in the study of Torah (עוֹסְקֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ) victorious over the Jews who had taken the side of the Greeks, adopted the immorality of Greek culture (טְמֵאִים) and רְשָׁעִים), and deliberately tried to eradicate Torah study (זֵדִים). All the world recognized Your power and greatness, and You brought about a great liberating victory for Your nation. Then Your children cleaned up and purified the Beis Hamikdash and lit the Menorah and instituted these eight days of Chanukah for giving thanks and praise to You.

In—בִּימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר On Purim: In the days of Mordechai and Esther, in the capital city of Shushan, the evil Haman rose up to exterminate all Jews, young and old, on the thirteenth day of Adar. But You in Your great mercy thwarted his plan and caused his scheme against us to boomerang onto his own head, and he and his sons were hung on the gallows.

וְעַל כֻּלָּם—Our King, for all these things may Your Name be blessed and held in the highest esteem (may everyone realize that You alone are the Source of hidden miracles and loving-kindness), constantly, forever and ever.
וּכְתֹב לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים—And may all the children of Your covenant with the Avos (that's us!) be written for a good life.

וְכֹל הַחַיִּים—And all that live will thank You forever; וִיהַלְלוּ—and sincerely praise all that You do; הָאֵל יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ—You are our salvation and everlasting help. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַטּוֹב שִׁמְךָ וּלְךָ נָאֶה לְהוֹדוֹת—Your very essence is goodness and benevolence, and therefore it is (always) fitting to thank You (in all circumstances of our lives, even if we cannot see the good at the moment).

—אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, please bless us with the threefold brachah written in the Torah that was said by the Kohanim:
—יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ May Hashem bless you (with material abundance) and protect you (from misusing it!).
—יָאֵר יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וִיחֻנֶּךָּ May Hashem grace you with sensitivity to spirituality so that you can see His providence (in your life).
—יִשָּׂא יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְיָשֵׂם לְךָ שָׁלוֹם May you feel the constant Presence of Hashem, and thus be at peace (within yourself).

(*Peace of mind, inner peace:*) שִׂים שָׁלוֹם טוֹבָה וּבְרָכָה—Hashem, grant each of us an inner sense of well-being (*by showering us with*) goodness, blessings, favor, loving-kindness, and compassion (*through which we can easily recognize the love You have for us; thus our soul will feel at peace with You*). And may this serenity extend to all members of Bnei Yisrael, Your nation.

(*Peace between one another:*) בָּרְכֵנוּ—Our Father, bless all of us together to become one unified nation, by allowing us to all equally see Your Presence (*and thanks to such clarity, discord will cease!*). For You, Hashem, when we were in Your direct Divine Presence (*at Har Sinai*), gave us a living Torah (*which teaches us how to live together in harmony*), and You also gave us a love of doing kindness and righteousness. (*This all leads to everyone sharing*) their blessings with each other, living with compassion, and thus having a full life and living in peace (*by forgiving others*).

(*Peace from war and danger:*) וְטוֹב בְּעֵינֶיךָ לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמְּךָ—And may it be favorable in Your eyes to bless Your people, Bnei Yisrael, at all times and at every moment, with Your peace (*protection from wars and dangers*).
בְּסֵפֶר חַיִּים—May we and Your entire nation, the family of Bnei Yisrael, be remembered and written in the book of life, brachah, peace, and prosperity, for a good life and for peace.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּשָּׁלוֹם—Who blesses His people, Bnei Yisrael, with (*all three forms of*) peace.
יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי—May all that I have said (*during this Shemoneh Esrei*) and all the thoughts in my heart be acceptable to You, Hashem, my rock and my redeemer.

Please, —אֱלֹהַי, נְצֹר לְשׁוֹנִי מֵרָע Hashem, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking with dishonesty. And to those who curse or insult me, let me have the ability to remain silent and not respond. Open my heart to Your
Torah so that my neshamah will desire and run after mitzvos. And all those who plot evil against me, Hashem, please nullify and thwart their plans.

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ—Please, Hashem, let no one be jealous of me, and may I not be jealous of others. Do not allow the yetzer hara to get the better of me, and help me stay humble (despite my accomplishments today) and not be arrogant. Please rebuild the Beis Hamikdash so that the whole world will recognize Your providence, and bring us all back to Yerushalayim.

עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ—Even though I may personally not be worthy, do this for the sake of Your holy Name and for the honor of Your Torah; because we are Your beloved children; therefore with strength and power save me and answer my requests. יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי—May all that I have said (during this Shemoneh Esrei) and all the thoughts in my heart be acceptable to You, Hashem, my rock and my redeemer. עֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו—May He Who makes peace in the Heavens (in the world of angels and in nature); הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ—may He bring about peace upon us (since we seem to have a hard time doing it ourselves, may Hashem impose peace upon us!); וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל; אָמֵן וְאִמְרוּ—and upon all of Bnei Yisrael; and (may the two angels who accompany me through life and therefore have been listening to my tefillah, please respond and) say Amen.

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ—May it be Your will, Hashem, Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, that the Beis Hamikdash be rebuilt quickly in our days, and help us find our unique connection to Your Torah. And there (in the Beis Hamikdash) we will

be able to serve You with proper respect, as it was in the days of old. (And when Mashiach arrives and rebuilds the Beis Hamikdash) then the korbanos of Yehudah and Yerushalayim will be accepted by Hashem, as it was in the days of old.

You control everything, and have taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history starting from the time of the Avos. Please accept our tefillos, and do not turn away from us, for we are not arrogant hypocrites claiming that we are perfect. Rather, we are being honest (with You and with ourselves), and we admit that we have not lived up to our potential!

This list of transgressions follows the order of the א-ב and is meant to help us think of specific areas that we need to work on. If Hebrew does not "work" for you, then simply think of specific things in both bein adam l'chaveiro (friends, parents) and bein adam la'Makom (tefillah, what you read, watch, and listen to) and talk to Hashem! Simply explain to Him that you are aware of what you need to work on and will try the best you can! And then say the next paragraph.

We have strayed from Your mitzvos, which we know You gave us for our own good; וְלֹא שָׁוָה לָנוּ—and those inappropriate activities are not befitting who we really are, for we are truly above such actions (which is why we are asking for time to improve so that we can live up to our true potential!).

You are slow to anger and are full of compassion (and thus we ask for time to get back on track). Please show us compassion and listen to our requests (for help in returning to You and living up to our true potential). You Yourself taught Moshe that we should proclaim
Your thirteen attributes of mercy (י"ג), (מדות הרחמים), and You will listen to our requests, forgive our mistakes, and give us another chance, as it says in the Torah:
And Hashem passed before Moshe and Hashem called out (that we should say the following in our tefillos):
He is compassionate before one has sinned. We need Hashem's mercy even before we ever sin, for Hashem owes us nothing! All that we have is only due to His mercy and compassion.

He is compassionate after one has sinned and done teshuvah. Unlike human beings, who tend to distance themselves from those who have wronged them, Hashem's closeness to us remains even after we have sinned (even seriously) against Him.
Hashem compassionately uses His might to restrain His anger and arouse His mercy.
He eases the punishment of sinners when they call out to Him.
He acts charitably to those who ask for it, even if they are unworthy.
He is slow to anger and does not punish us immediately—in the hope that we will improve.
He shows great chessed to those who need it but do not necessarily deserve it by their own merit.

The terms מושיע, עוזר, and מגן represent three levels of help that we need in our lives — from the least to the most. עוזר — "help," is when we are on the right track, doing what we need to do in the best way possible, and we ask Hashem to please help us that all should work out, since nothing will come to fruition without His help. מושיע — "salvation," is when we are completely at a loss; we throw up our hands and say to Hashem, "Save me, I have no idea what to do next!" The third and highest level, מגן — "protect," is when we think we're on the right track and think we know what we're doing, but in truth we are completely off base! We ask Hashem, "If I'm going in the wrong direction — מגן — protect me from myself!"

יש אומרים כאן תפילה זו:

Instant Insight: Why do we say, "Listen to our voice (קולנו)"? Shouldn't we ask Hashem to listen to the words we say? What we are asking Hashem is: "I may not be so articulate, and I may not know how to say what I really feel. But I hope You can tell from the sound of my voice that I am doing the best I can to communicate with You!"

Crucial Instant Insight: We asked Hashem to "accept our tefillos," so what are we adding by requesting, "Do not turn us away empty-handed"? Of course, we hope that Hashem will grant us what we have requested. But sometimes, for reasons known only to Him, Hashem must say no. We therefore ask Hashem that if the answer to our tefillah must be a no, at least He should not send us away feeling "empty-handed"—with a feeling of total rejection. Let our hearts be filled with emunah that we had the amazing zechus and opportunity to talk one-on-one with Hashem and that He heard our tefillah, even if the best thing for us right now is a no.

spans.text: By all other brachos of the Shemoneh Esrei, we simply respond "Amen" to the chazzan's brachah. Why here must we say our own "Modim," as if an Amen is not sufficient? All other brachos are requests. When you are with someone else and they put in a request for something important, saying simply, "And me too—I also agree!" is fine. He represents you. That is Amen. But if someone is really bursting with gratitude, especially to Hashem, for "our lives, which are entrusted into Your Hand" and "for our miraculous survival till today," then Amen is impossible. No one can "represent" your inner feeling of gratitude! It must burst forth! Thus, Modim D'Rabbanan!

Birkas Kohanim is said by the chazzan (and in some places in Israel by Kohanim) during the repetition of the Shemoneh Esrei:

Instant Insight: Generally, we think of "שלום—peace" as meaning people getting along with each other. But if so, then the third brachah should have said "וישם לכם Hashem will—שלום give peace to you," plural, i.e., to the group. Why is the word "לך—to you," singular, used? The singular is used because you cannot get along with others if you first do not get along with yourself! Thus, this brachah is to the individual—that each person should have inner serenity and peace. Only then can we live in peace with others.
